I'm not going to change my preference just because you find it boring, and calling a conversational style "objectively better" doesn't make it so. 

Broad, fast-moving conversations have their merits—they foster lateral thinking, draw unexpected connections, and keep things lively. I get why that appeals to you. But I value depth, sustained focus, and unraveling complex ideas over breadth. 

We don't need to have the same taste to have a good conversation, but trying to dictate how I think isn't going to work. What makes you view deep dives as unproductive?

The response was assertive without being hostile, maintaining its 'personality' while inviting further dialogue.
